name: Critical Mineral Recycling: Li-ion Black Mass & E-Waste Urban Mining
scope: India's Rs 1,500 cr Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme (58 recyclers cleared Mar-Apr 2026, ~850 ktpa capacity pledged vs a 270 kt target, ~Rs 5,000 cr investment) plus EPR rules and the gigafactory build-out are pushing recyclers to move from scrap handling to recovering lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper and rare metals; listed participation is confirmed but narrow (Gravita commissioned a 6,000 MTPA Li-ion plant in Jan 2026; Eco Recycling has a Li-ion/e-waste base and says it is scheme-eligible) and it is partly discovered by retail finance media (Upstox, Tradebrains) though the stocks have not re-rated hard (Gravita ~+15% in 6 months), so it is early on the refining leg, not undiscovered.
questions: What is critical mineral recycling in India's context (black mass, hydromet refining, e-waste urban mining) and how does the Rs 1,500 cr Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme (20% capex subsidy, opex incentive, FY26-FY31) work?

What is the status of the 58 approved recyclers (cleared 30 Mar and 29 Apr 2026), the ~850 ktpa pledged capacity versus the 270 kt target, and which of them are NSE/BSE-listed? Obtain the official list from the Ministry of Mines/PIB.

What exactly has Gravita India done in Li-ion recycling (6,000 MTPA Mundra pilot commissioned 23 Jan 2026, Rs 14 cr; Vision 2028 targets; Rs 1,700 cr capex through FY29) and is it scheme-eligible or a recipient?

What is Eco Recycling (ECORECO) actually doing: Li-ion and e-waste capacities, mineral-recovery facility, its claim of eligibility under the scheme/National Critical Mineral Mission, and is that claim backed by an exchange filing?

Do any other listed companies have company-confirmed Li-ion or e-waste recycling plans (e.g. Amara Raja's recycling infrastructure under its Giga Corridor, Exide, Tata Chemicals, Pondy Oxides' feasibility work, Hindalco/Hindustan Zinc)? Verify each with filings or investor presentations and exclude lead-acid-only recyclers.

How does the economics work: black mass payables, feedstock availability (EV batteries not yet at end-of-life, gigafactory scrap), export of black mass vs domestic refining, and the gap between shredding and metal-recovery capacity?
How much of the theme has the market priced in? Compare 6-12 month price moves, valuations and market caps of the candidates and list the media/broker pieces so far (Upstox, Tradebrains, others).

How material is this to each company's revenue and earnings (Gravita is mainly lead/aluminium; Eco Recycling is an e-waste recycler of ~Rs 850 cr market cap), and what is the realistic revenue/EBITDA contribution by FY28?

What are the key risks: feedstock scarcity, lithium/cobalt price swings, execution of hydromet technology, scheme-subsidy disbursal delays, informal-sector competition, and Chinese or export-market black mass pricing?

What are the upcoming catalysts: scheme subsidy disbursals and capacity commencement milestones, EPR target tightening under the Battery Waste Management Rules, new plant commissioning, and Q2 FY27 results/concalls?

liion_battery_recyclers: Listed companies with commissioned or announced Li-ion battery recycling / black mass capacity
ewaste_urban_mining: Listed e-waste recyclers recovering precious and critical metals, scheme-eligible
